_: Liquid water at skin temperature (32-37 C): the base of sweat, tears and saliva and of the wet state. Sources: the project's materials research note GAPS_RESEARCH.md 5. Materials foundation lane 2026-11-07. v2 (world lane, 2026-11-07): contact / deform / thermal added; the old `mechanics` block moved into them; layers, surface and variants untouched. States: ice, vapour (steam, fog), film, droplet.

thickness_mm.src: a droplet or film's own size

f_water.src: pure water (POPEFRY97, spectra.json): 0.0092 / 0.0565 / 0.325 per m at 450 / 550 / 650 nm - clear at mm scale

n.src: DAIMON07 Sellmeier at 550 nm, 20 C (1.3396 at 450, 1.3317 at 650); ~1.331 at 37 C (dn/dT ~ -1.5e-4, E)

alpha.src: a free liquid surface is smooth at optical scale (capillary waves only)

surface_tension_mN_m.src: IAPWS 2014 correlation (GAPS 5 evaluated 25/32/37 C; 20 C from the same formula)

viscosity_mPa_s.src: IAPWS 2008 (GAPS 5 Vogel fit for 32/37 C; 20/25 C standard IAPWS values); model newtonian

density_kg_m3.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: 999.975 (4 C), 998.207 (20 C), 993.330 (37 C) kg/m3

water_contact_angle_deg.src: GAPS MAVON97, ELKHYAT04 (via secondary); sweat puddles 20-40 deg: research/skin_moisture.md T3. Sebum makes skin MORE wettable (MAVON97)

wetting.note: angles on other solids (glass, marble, wood, cotton) are pair values: pairs/world.json

porous_solids.v: water enters any porous solid with a contact angle < 90 deg by capillary suction (Washburn: depth ~ sqrt(gamma r cos(theta) t / (2 mu))); wood, sandstone, unglazed stone, soil and cotton take it up; the permeability_m2 and water_absorption of each solid live in that solid's profile

stratum_corneum_swelling.v: the stratum corneum takes up water and swells in thickness (corneocytes swell; at full hydration the SC is several times its dry mass and markedly thicker); fingertip/palm glabrous skin wrinkles after minutes of warm immersion
stratum_corneum_swelling.src: BOUWSTRA03: E: recalled from Bouwstra 2003, not re-read (SC swells in thickness with hydration); wrinkling onset ~5-10 min at ~40 C is E from the immersion-wrinkling literature

skin_friction_effect.v: a thin water film on skin RAISES skin friction against most counterfaces (softened SC, more real contact, capillary adhesion) until the film is thick enough to lubricate

friction.v: a liquid: no friction of its own; it changes the friction of the pair it wets (see states.film and pairs/world.json)

v.film_on_surface: the film's own thickness (layers / film values)

collision_thickness_mm.src: ANON_E solver convention: a liquid has no skin of its own; it keeps a no-penetration boundary at solids

model.v: incompressible: no stiffness ramp; a pressure projection (or weakly compressible SPH with numerical sound speed >= 10x the max flow speed) keeps it out of solids and out of itself
model.src: bulk modulus (water 2.2 GPa: effectively incompressible at body speeds)

boundary_wetting.v: the contact angle per pair (pairs/world.json wetting) sets the meniscus at a solid

restitution.src: RICHARD02 / DEGENNES04: drops stick and spread on wettable solids; bounce only on (super)hydrophobic ones

response_time_ms.src: RICHARD02 tau = 2.6 sqrt(rho R^3/gamma) with rho 994, gamma 0.0705 N/m

wave_speed_m_s.src: sound ~ water's (CRC; oils ~1450); capillary-wave phase speed sqrt(2 pi gamma/(rho lambda)) at lambda 1 mm

damping_ratio.v: viscous: set by viscosity_mPa_s (no separate damping)

density_kg_m3.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: 994.37 at 34 C, 993.33 at 37 C (994 at ~35 C)

bulk_modulus_GPa.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: adiabatic K = rho c^2 = 998.207 x 1482.35^2 = 2.19 GPa at 20 C; 2.2 kept (the isothermal value from CRC compressibility is recalled, not re-read)

sound_speed_m_s.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: 1482.35 (20 C), 1523.66 (37 C) m/s

capillary_length_mm.src: DEGENNES04 l_c = sqrt(gamma/(rho g)) with gamma 72.0 mN/m, rho 998, g 9.80665

sim.note: SPH/FLIP: use the real viscosity only at mm scale; at body scale numerical viscosity dominates

conductivity_W_mK.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: 0.5980 (20 C), 0.6245 (37 C) W/mK; 37 C corrected from 0.627

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: cp 4184 (20 C), 4179 (34-37 C) J/kgK; IT'IS v5.0 water 4178 (re-read 11-08); 4178 kept

emissivity.src: CRC: E: recalled from CRC / IR thermography tables (0.95-0.98), not re-read

latent_heat_vaporisation_kJ_kg.src: NISTWB (NIST Chemistry WebBook, IAPWS-95 / IAPWS 2011 formulations, 0.101325 MPa), re-read 11-08: h_vap = h_v - h_l at saturation: 2564.55 - 146.63 = 2417.9 (35 C), 2675.57 - 419.17 = 2256.4 (100 C); 100 C corrected from 2257

latent_heat_fusion_kJ_kg.src: CRC: E: recalled from the CRC Handbook (333.6 kJ/kg), not re-read

film_um.src: research/eye.md F1 precorneal film 3.3 +- 1.5 um; lipid layer 52.7 nm

set.contact.premelt: a nm-thick liquid-like layer exists below 0 C (thicker toward 0 C); at speed, frictional melting adds a meltwater film; the film is ~ 100x more viscous than bulk water (CANALE19); hence ice is slippery near 0 C and grippier when very cold

ice.src: density 917 / k 2.22 / cp 2.05: CRC; n 1.309 at 589 nm: WARREN08; E ~9 GPa (9-10 GPa, polycrystal), nu 0.31-0.36, strengths, K_IC: PETROVIC03; shear D = E/(2(1+nu)); effusivity D; friction ranges KIETZIG10 / CANALE19 (E within those reviews' ranges: slow sliding high, fast low); premelt PREMELT; alpha E (smooth melt-glazed ice; frosted/rimed ice much rougher); solver: phase solid, 10 um numerical skin (E: smooth hard solid), shear wave sqrt(G/rho) D, restitution of ice spheres on ice 0.3-0.7 at ~1 m/s (planetary-ring impact experiments, Bridges et al. 1984 Nature 309:333, recalled; frost lowers it) E

set.optics.steam_visible: pure vapour is invisible (n - 1 ~ 2.5e-4 like air); visible 'steam' is condensed droplets of a few to tens of um

vapour.src: steam and saturation densities: CRC steam tables; fog/mist droplet sizes and LWC: PRUPPACHER (recalled ranges); Koschmieder relation standard (D)

set.contact.film_effect.on_skin: raises skin friction vs dry (GERHARDT08: wet skin on textiles roughly x1.5-2+) by softening and capillary adhesion
set.contact.film_effect.on_hard_smooth: lubricates: hydrodynamic film under a sliding rubber/hard pair (hydroplaning); shoe/tyre COF ~0.6-0.9 dry -> ~0.2-0.5 wet on smooth floors
set.contact.film_effect.on_rough_porous: little change on rough drained surfaces (asphalt, textured stone), large on polished stone, glazed tile, ice
set.contact.film_breakup: a film thinner than ~ the capillary length on a surface with contact angle > 0 dewets into droplets (DEGENNES04)

film.src: GERHARDT08 (skin); PERSSON (rubber, floors; recalled ranges); dewetting DEGENNES04; thickness range E (from a molecular film to a 1 mm sheet)

set.bond_number: Bo = rho g L^2 / gamma = (L / 2.71 mm)^2: Bo < 1 drops stay round (sessile caps), Bo > 1 they flatten into puddles of height ~ 2 l_c sin(theta/2)
set.rain_drop_shape: spherical below ~1 mm; oblate 'hamburger bun' above ~2 mm; break up above ~6-8 mm

droplet.src: capillary length / Bond / puddle height D from DEGENNES04 formulas with IAPWS gamma; terminal velocities GUNNKINZER49 (recalled standard table); shapes and break-up PRUPPACHER

IAPWS.cite: IAPWS releases: Surface Tension of Ordinary Water Substance (2014); Viscosity of Ordinary Water (2008); IAPWS-95 density; thermal conductivity (2011)
IAPWS.lic: freely available releases; numbers used as facts

CRC.cite: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (any recent edition): standard property tables for water, ice, air, oils. Values recalled as standard table values, not re-checked line by line this session
CRC.lic: copyright, paywalled; individual physical constants used as facts, no table copied

PETROVIC03.cite: Petrovic JJ. Review: Mechanical properties of ice and snow. J Mater Sci 38:1-6 (2003). doi:10.1023/A:1021134128038. Values recalled, not re-checked

WARREN08.cite: Warren SG, Brandt RE. Optical constants of ice from the ultraviolet to the microwave: a revised compilation. J Geophys Res 113:D14220 (2008); via refractiveindex.info
WARREN08.lic: database CC0 1.0; paper's numbers used as facts

KIETZIG10.cite: Kietzig A-M, Hatzikiriakos SG, Englezos P. Physics of ice friction. J Appl Phys 107:081101 (2010). doi:10.1063/1.3340792. Regimes (premelt / meltwater film) read from the abstract; numbers are typical ranges from the review literature, recalled

CANALE19.cite: Canale L, Comtet J, Nigues A, et al. Nanorheology of interfacial water during ice gliding. Phys Rev X 9:041025 (2019)

GUNNKINZER49.cite: Gunn R, Kinzer GD. The terminal velocity of fall for water droplets in stagnant air. J Meteorol 6:243-248 (1949). Values recalled as widely tabulated

PRUPPACHER.cite: Pruppacher HR, Klett JD. Microphysics of Clouds and Precipitation, 2nd ed. Kluwer (1997): fog/cloud droplet sizes, raindrop break-up. Recalled
PRUPPACHER.lic: book, copyright; numbers used as facts
